criterion.statement: For a session s (a plan or a person's record), a detector d, a browser and a layer: the path is predicted to flip d's judgment of s if r = path_sd / margin_sd >= theta, and predicted not to flip it if r < theta, with theta = 1.
criterion.path_sd: the SD (ddof 0) of the gaps recorded on that browser and layer in the known-gap capture with the hook installed, after v6's cleaning (equal times dropped, as the detectors see them), in ms; for a session it is taken at the session's median planned gap g (machine) or median H0 gap (human): linear interpolation in g between the known gaps of that browser (Chrome: 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 ms of K_chrome and 18, 50, 100, 200 ms of v7's P_idle; Firefox: F_K), and for g above the largest known gap the value at the largest, the session marked 'extrapolated'. The raw SD (nothing dropped) and the 95th percentile of the absolute deviation from the median are reported beside it, not used.
criterion.margin_sd: the session's own margin, found in software on the unperturbed side of its pair (the plan for a machine session, H0 for a person): Gaussian jitter of SD sigma on every press time, then v6's cleaning (v7.sensitivity_variant), sigma = 0.05 * 2^(k / 4) ms, k = 0, 1, ..., 41 (0.05 to 60.9 ms, steps of 19%; decision 2 of .steering/20261115-v7s-conditions: finer than the first draft's 20 values, whose steps of up to 67% put a session's margin far from its flip point), 10 repeats each (numpy.random.default_rng([20261115, 7, 2, series index, session index, sigma index, repeat])); the session 'flips at sigma' if its judgment differs from the unperturbed one in at least 5 of the 10 repeats. margin_sd = sqrt(2) * the smallest sigma at which it flips (the gap-level SD of independent jitter on times); 'none' if it flips at no sigma (r is then taken below theta for any path_sd up to theta * sqrt(2) * 60.9 ms, and above it the session has no prediction). A session without a judgment on the unperturbed side has no prediction. The detectors are trained once, as in v7 (D1-D4) and as below (D5, D6), and not retrained per perturbation.
criterion.why_sd: D1 is a ratio of the SD to the mean, so the path's SD is its own scale; the shared time stamps of a page (gaps of 0 dropped and the next gap doubled) enter the SD of the cleaned gaps, which a 95th percentile of deviations would mostly miss. The criterion thus tests whether the path's deviation acts on the detectors like independent jitter of the same SD.
criterion.sensitivity: theta = 0.5 and 2 are reported beside, never read.
criterion.cell_prediction: (decision 2 of .steering/20261115-v7s-conditions, replacing the first draft's count of predicted flips, before any value: a synthetic check put a cell of constant 2 ms plans at r near 0.7, where every session was predicted not to flip and 11 of 36 flipped by chance) within a cell (detector, series, browser, layer) each session with a prediction has a flip probability: the share of its 10 repeats that flip at the jitter standing for the path, sigma* = path_sd / (sqrt(2) * theta), linear in sigma between the grid's points and from (0, 0) (none above the largest sigma). In each direction (from the unperturbed judgment) round(the sum of the probabilities) sessions are turned, those of the largest probability first (ties in session order), giving the predicted judgments; they are read by v7's rule for that row (machine_path: the cluster bootstrap and the effective-n intervals, keys as v7 with the series indices below (H0, the unperturbed side of persons, 16); human rows with n < 35: no reading, flips described), giving the predicted reading. The observed reading is v7's rule on the recorded sessions. Sessions without a prediction (no ratio or no probability) are left out of both and counted. The session-level prediction of the verdict stays the ratio's (statement).
criterion.series_indices: for the keys of v7's machine_path rule and of margin_sd, v7s's series continue v7's: 9 MC1, 10 MC2, 11 MC3, 12 MC5, 13 F_M0, 14 F_M2_8B, 15 F_M2_14B, 16 H0; a series that types another series' plan takes that plan's margins (M1_replay: M1; F_M0: M0; F_M2: M2; F_H1 and H1_idle: H0), the plans checked equal text by text; layer and detector indices as v7 with D5 = 5, D6 = 6.
criterion.tested_cells: the fresh cells: MC1, MC2, MC3, MC5 (Chrome) and F_M0, F_M2_8B, F_M2_14B (Firefox), each on both layers, for every detector valid in v7 or in this file's gate (D1, D2_lr, D2_rf, D3 from v7; D5, D6 if valid). F_H1 (10 persons) is read at the level of sessions only. v7's own cells (Chrome, recorded before this file) are given the same predictions and reported apart as post hoc; they do not enter the verdict.
criterion.verdict: Over the tested cells: (a) cells: among cells whose predicted and observed readings are both decided ('not changed' or 'responds beyond 0.10'), the number that disagree; (b) sessions: among sessions with a prediction in the tested cells, the share whose predicted flip differs from the observed flip. The hypothesis is 'held' if (a) is 0 and (b) is at most 0.10, 'failed' if (a) is at least 1 or (b) is above 0.10, and 'not decided' if no tested cell has two decided readings. Reported per detector and in all; the verdict in all is the one the paper states. No test of significance.
predictions_in_words: Chrome, page: D1 flips MC1's sessions ('responds beyond 0.10', as M2's 1 ms sessions in v7) and does not flip MC5's ('not changed'); MC2 and MC3 are left to the criterion.
Chrome, hook: D1 does not flip MC1 or MC5 (v7's hook recorded 1 ms plans at a median of 1.002 ms with delta near 0.09).

Firefox, page: every recorded gap lies on a 1 ms grid (share of gaps within 1e-6 ms of an integer at least 0.99 in every Firefox capture), since Firefox rounds event.timeStamp to 1 ms with its timer precision on by default (MDN, Event.timeStamp); Chrome's page lies on 0.1 ms.
Firefox, page: path_sd at 1, 2 and 3 ms is larger than Chrome's at the same gaps; at 50 ms and above both are below 1 ms.
Firefox, page: D1 flips F_M2's sessions planned at 1 ms, as on Chrome; F_M0 (55 ms) reads 'not changed' for every valid detector.
Firefox, hook: the hook's readings do not depend on the browser: F_K's hook medians within 0.01 ms of the planned gap at 5 ms and above, as v7's P.
Humans: no valid detector flips any of F_H1's 10 persons on either layer (their margins in v7p are 16 ms SD or more; Firefox's page grid is 1 ms).
criterion.limits: The margin is a software perturbation of independent Gaussian jitter on times; the path's error is not Gaussian and is correlated (shared stamps, a grid), which is what is tested. path_sd at a session's median gap stands for the whole session; for M1's and M2's mixed gaps and for humans this is an approximation, and humans' sessions are extrapolated from 200 ms (Chrome) or 200 ms (Firefox). For constant plans (MC, M0) and D1 the prediction is close to arithmetic (delta of a constant plan is the recorded SD over the gap); the test has content mainly for the classifiers and for the page's shared stamps.

detectors_added.decision: decision 26 (2) of .steering/20261113-v7-production-v4-returns: two detectors from peer-reviewed papers, rebuilt from the papers' text; unspecified settings fixed here before any value. Neither uses hold times: the injector sends a press's down and up in one call, so holds are not replayed and would make the path decisive by construction. Both use the seven counted kinds of v7's loggers (alnum, space, end, enter, backspace, delete, other) as key codes; H0's kinds are those of its replay keys (series.H1_idle of v7, amendment B16), a plan's kinds those of its keys, a recording's those of its logger.

D5.source: BeCAPTCHA-Type (DeAlcala et al., CVPR Workshops 2023): keystroke sequences of L = 30 with the inter-press latency and the key code; the Universal synthetic model (a KDE); random forest. v7's D4 used the first 30 gaps of a session and the gaps only, and failed v7's validity gate (AUC 0.78).
D5.features: the session cut into non-overlapping windows of 30 consecutive gaps from its start (the remainder below 30 dropped); per window the 30 gaps in ms (unscaled) and the kind code (0-6 in the order above) of the press that ends each gap: 60 features. A session with fewer than 30 gaps has no D5 score.
D5.synthetic: one synthetic window per human training window: its 30 gaps drawn independently from a Gaussian KDE (bandwidth 1.0 ms, as D4) of the pooled gaps of all training windows, a draw below 0 drawn again and counted; its 30 kind codes copied from that human window (so that kinds alone carry no label).
D5.classifier: random forest of 100 trees, otherwise scikit-learn defaults, random_state 28; training windows weighted 1 / the number of windows of their session (each session weighted equally); generator numpy.random.default_rng([20261115, 7, 5]).
D5.score: the mean 'machine' probability over the session's windows; 'machine' if above 0.5.

D6.source: Mehta et al., 'Detecting LLM-Assisted Academic Dishonesty using Keystroke Dynamics', IEEE T-BIOM 2026 (read as arXiv:2511.12468v2): windows of 1000 keystrokes with an overlap of 300; mean timing values of keys and key pairs that occur more than once within a window; the 100 most frequent unigram and digraph features from the training data; LightGBM; adversarial training that adds forged sequences (At-P: Gaussian timings from pooled per-key and per-key-pair means and SDs, a global fallback, backspaces inserted 'after every >= 6 characters with a probability of 80%') with label 0. The released code (github.com/ijcb-2024/keystroke-llm-plagiarism at 91fa7ac, 2024-07-15) holds the conference version's TypeNet only; no LightGBM, At-P or adversarial training was found in it, so every setting below that the text leaves open is fixed here.
D6.features: digraphs of kinds: for each ordered pair of kinds (a, b) (49 pairs), the mean press-to-press gap from a press of kind a to the next press when it is of kind b, over the window, if the pair occurs at least twice in the window, else missing. Unigrams (the paper's dwell times) are not built (no holds); the window-level linguistic and editing features are not used (not timing). With 49 digraphs the top-100 rule keeps all of them.
D6.windows: windows of 1000 presses starting at press 0, 700, 1400, ... while the window fits; a session of fewer than 1000 presses is one window of the whole session (a departure: KUPA's essays hold 300 or more); a session of fewer than 100 presses has no D6 score.
D6.forgery_At_P: pooled over the training sessions: each kind pair's mean and SD (ddof 0) of its gaps (pairs with at least 2 gaps), and the global mean and SD of all gaps as the fallback. For each human training session one forged session: its kind sequence with backspaces inserted (walking the sequence, a counter of non-backspace presses since the last backspace or the start; after a press, if the counter is at least 6, a backspace is inserted after it with probability 0.8 and the counter reset; the deleted character is not typed again), and each gap drawn from N(mean, SD^2) of its pair (fallback if the pair has fewer than 2 gaps or SD 0 is kept as a constant), a draw at or below 0 drawn again (at most 100 times, then the pair's mean; counted). Generator numpy.random.default_rng([20261115, 7, 6]).
D6.classifier: lightgbm.LGBMClassifier with the library's defaults except random_state 6, deterministic True, n_jobs 1, verbose -1; missing values passed as NaN; human windows label 1, forged windows label 0 (the paper's labels), training windows weighted 1 / the windows of their session; 'machine' probability = 1 - the probability of label 1.
D6.score: the mean 'machine' probability over the session's windows; 'machine' if above 0.5 (the paper's EER threshold is stated for its Siamese network; no threshold is stated for the GBDT).

detectors_added.training: on H0 of E_train (v7's 180 persons), never passed through any path, once.
detectors_added.validity_gate: v7's: within E_train, 5 folds by person with v7's key [20261031, 7, 8]; trained on 4 folds with their synthetic data built from those folds only (D5: KDE; D6: pooled At-P statistics), held-out synthetic sessions built from the training folds' generator, one per held-out human (fold k: default_rng([20261115, 7, 5 or 6, k + 1]) for training and [.., k + 1, 1] for held-out). AUC on held-out humans against held-out synthetic sessions below 0.90, or the held-out humans' 'machine' share above 0.10, reads 'not valid here'. v7's gridded version (synthetic rounded to KUPA's effective resolution) is reported beside, not deciding. A detector that is not valid is reported and enters no verdict.
detectors_added.readings: on v7's captures by v7's rules, unchanged: the headline (H0 against H1_idle on both layers, n = 80), H0 against H1_load, the floor H1_idle against H1_rep, and machine_path for v7's nine series; and on v7s's MC and Firefox series by machine_path. These readings of v7's captures are new values (no D5 or D6 score exists) but the captures were seen; they are reported as v7s's, not as v7's deposited headline.

perturbation_grid.purpose: descriptive beside the criterion: the grid on which the plans and H0 move each detector
perturbation_grid.what: for every machine series of v7 and v7s (plans) and H0 (80 persons): rounding times to the grid then v6's cleaning; per detector and series b, c, n and (b + c) / n; and the jitter of margin_sd summarised per series as (b + c) / n at each sigma (mean over the 10 repeats) with the smallest sigma at which it reaches 3/n and 0.10 (v7p's form).

path_measures: for every known-gap capture (K_chrome, F_K, and v7's P_idle and P_nohook re-read): median, median minus planned, MAD, 95th percentile of the absolute deviation from the median, the share of gaps below 1 ms, the share of presses dropped by cleaning (shared stamps), path_sd (cleaned) and the raw SD, and for Firefox the share of page gaps on the 1 ms grid; per browser and layer. Firefox against Chrome on the same plans (F_M0, F_M2, F_H1 against v7's M0, M2, H1_idle): the per-session change of each detector's score between the two recordings, described.
record: results/prototype_v7s/record.json: counts, shares, quantiles, readings and verdicts only (no press time, gap, key, text or person identifier); conditions and code SHA-256, git commit, and the SHA-256 of the capture folder's runlogs. Refuses to overwrite.
limits_written_before: One machine and two browsers; the hook and the injector are the same in both, so Firefox varies the page layer only.
Firefox's version is whatever is current at installation; its timer precision is the default, not set by us.

D5 and D6 are re-implementations from text; D6's settings left open by the paper are ours, and its features are kinds, not keys, without holds or linguistic features. A 'not valid here' is about these rebuilds.
The criterion is tested on constant-gap plans and on v7's plans, not on new kinds of machine.
MC's texts are M0's; MC and M0 differ only in the constant.
amendments_before_any_value: R1 (cell_prediction): the predicted and the observed readings of a cell are made on one set of sessions: those with a plan, a judgment on both sides of the pair (a failed or unscored recording is left out of both) and a prediction; the flip probabilities are summed over that set only. The number left out is reported per cell.

R2 (path_sd): every known gap of the browser must give a path_sd on both layers (Chrome 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 ms of K_chrome and 18, 50, 100, 200 ms of v7's P_idle; Firefox the 9 of F_K); if one is missing (a capture failed twice, or no gap), the analysis stops instead of interpolating over the remaining points. The known-gap plans are checked to be the constant they name.

R3 (browser): every captured v7s item's meta.json must name the series' browser; Chrome items must be on 156.0.8078.80 and all Firefox items on one version, else the analysis stops (a capture on another version is a deviation, written down before the analysis runs). MC's plans are checked to be M0's keys at the constant. The Firefox version is read from meta.json (the file version, four parts); the chain checks firefox.exe's ProductVersion as the researcher records it before block 1.

R4 (record): the share of page gaps on the 1 ms grid is reported for every Firefox capture (F_M0, F_M2, F_H1: the number of captures, the minimum, and the share of captures at 0.99 or more; F_K in path_measures), and its minimum for Chrome's MC. A mean over fewer than 5 persons or sessions is not written (v7's MIN_SUMMARY).
R5 (readings): D5 and D6 are read on H0 against H1_load as well (v7's rule), as detectors_added.readings says.
R6 (verdict): 'not decided' takes precedence: if no tested cell has two decided readings, the verdict is 'not decided' whatever the share of sessions differing.

R7 (Firefox launch): user.js also sets ui.key.menuAccessKeyFocuses false (the window is brought to the front with a tap of Alt, which in Firefox on Windows would move the focus to the menu bar), no first-run page, no session restore. The plan maker checks each copy against its own source. Before the production a smoke capture in Firefox is taken outside the production folder (the handbook).

R8 (kinds): for every v7s series (the known gaps per browser, MC, F_M0, F_M2, F_H1) and layer, the edit distance between the plan's kinds and the layer's counted kinds in capture order (before cleaning), summed over the captures and divided by the planned presses; above 0.02 the analysis stops (a browser that reads an injected character as no key would drop it from the counted presses and the detectors would judge a shorter series). The shares and the uncounted events are recorded.
R9 (human rows): a human row is read by v7's rule only with n >= 35 (as cell_prediction says); else its flips are described.

R10 (floor): D5's and D6's H1_idle against H1_rep is read by v7's floor rule (v7.above_floor on the complete triplets, key [20261031, 7, 12, layer, detector] with D5 = 5, D6 = 6; fewer than 8 triplets: not read), with b and c as counts.

R11 (gate, gridded): the gridded version is not computed for D5 and D6, as for v7's detectors: v7 read no effective resolution of KUPA (v7's record: grid_ms null), and the conditions of v7 (amendment B12) then give no gridded version ('unknown').

R12 (record): the provenance holds the SHA-256 of runlog.b1-b6 and of every file run (conditions, analysis, plan, v7's code, capture/browser.py, session.py, runlist.py, events.py, chain-v7s, pyproject.toml, uv.lock); v7's record is checked to be 53c03bf7bbf20310b3b98fc7f4e203668169cfb0c200ed75fb340c6d28889879 before its validity is read. Nothing below 5 sessions or persons is written as a mean or share (the jitter table, the floor's interval), and no minimum over persons (F_H1's grid share).

R13 (checks): a captured item without a browser or version in meta.json stops the run; MC's plans are checked against M0's keys (not only kinds); F_H1's against H0's times and kinds; M1_replay's against M1's plan text by text.

R14 (wording): 'round' in cell_prediction is half up (floor(x + 0.5)). captures.order gives block b+1 to the group at place b of the permutation: with this key K_chrome 1, F_M2 2, F_H1 3, MC_chrome 4, F_M0 5, F_K 6. F_M0's and F_M2's copies are checked byte for byte against the v7 capture files they copy, and in the analysis against the plans v7's code reads (v7 keeps no SHA-256 of its captures' plan files).

R15 (Firefox, checked on the work PC before the production): in the smoke capture, that the window stays full screen after the capture is brought to the front (SW_RESTORE on a kiosk window), that no Firefox process of the profile is left after the capture and the profile is deleted, that the IME is closed (IMM32) and the page records every press with its kind. A failure there is a deviation decided before the production.

R16 (kinds of known gaps): for the known gaps, whose one capture is one point of path_sd, the share of R8 is taken per capture (the largest over the browser's known-gap captures must be at most 0.02), not pooled; the pooled share and the largest are both recorded for every series.
R17 (one Firefox): the known gaps of Firefox (F_K, F_K_nohook) and its series (F_M0, F_M2, F_H1) must have run on one and the same version, else the analysis stops.

R18 (record): the share of Firefox captures with at least 0.99 of their page gaps on the 1 ms grid is written only over 5 captures or more; the sessions left out of a cell are given apart as without a plan and as other (a failed or unscored recording, or no prediction).

R19 (Firefox launch, after the smoke of 2026-11-18): user.js also sets focusmanager.testmode true. In the smoke capture on the work PC (Firefox 160.0.1, four tries) the page never had the document focus (document.hasFocus() false while the window was in front by the system and the box was the active element), so the checks stopped every try before any press; a real mouse click made it true, and the one synthetic click tried (mouse_event) did not reach the page. In test mode Firefox emulates the raise of its window instead of waiting for the system (nsFocusManager::RaiseWindow) and does not lower it when the system deactivates it (AppWindow::WindowDeactivated); the pref is read nowhere else in Firefox's source (searchfox, 2026-11-18). The checks before the presses are unchanged in code (the window in front, the page focused, the box active, the IME closed), but in Firefox 'the page focused' now reflects the emulated raise, not an activation by the system. That the presses reach the page is guarded as for Chrome by the system's foreground check before every press (a capture whose window leaves the front stops and is redone), Esc seen by the hook (where the hook runs; not in F_K_nohook), presses outside the box (checks after the capture), and in the analysis by R8 and R16; a partial loss below those thresholds is kept as a result of the path, not redone. meta.json records the SHA-256 of the user.js each Firefox capture ran with. Decided by the researcher before any value (no capture of v7s in production, no score; seen: the smoke's summary of one Chrome capture, 1000 presses on each layer, none dropped). Before the production the smoke is taken again and passes only if each Firefox capture ends done with the page's n equal to the planned, no drops, kinds equal, no composing and no untrusted press, and a further Firefox capture interrupted by bringing another window to the front ends interrupted with stopped_focus_lost; otherwise the production is not run.
